query: How can educators improve learning satisfaction?

per_column.name: teacher_instructional_quality
per_column.rationale: Directly relevant axis for how educators can improve satisfaction; distinguishes adaptive vs minimal teaching. Values are well-grounded readings (e.g. ED-0002 'creative/adaptive' -> high_adaptive; ED-0003 teacher can't tell she's lost -> low_minimal_effort). ED-0001 'adequate_routine' is a defensible read though the source mostly cites tech issues rather than teacher effort.

per_column.name: differentiation_support
per_column.rationale: Strong analytical axis for improving satisfaction via individualized support. Some values are inferential beyond the text: ED-0002 'moderate_office_hours' invents an office-hours specific not stated; ED-0001/ED-0004 'minimal_generic' is a weak-evidence default. ED-0003 'absent' is well grounded (teacher can't tell when she's lost).

per_column.name: content_delivery_format
per_column.rationale: Useful format dimension to compare satisfaction across modalities. Mostly grounded (ED-0004 recorded lectures + clips, ED-0002 project-based). But ED-0003 labeled 'mixed' when text only mentions a worksheet/reading platform, and ED-0004 'mixed' despite text describing recorded lectures only — some values not clearly warranted.

per_column.name: peer_social_learning_quality
per_column.rationale: Peer interaction is a distinct, actionable driver of satisfaction. Values are soundly derived: ED-0003 'zero peer interaction' -> absent; ED-0005 silent chat/cameras off -> absent; ED-0001 'thin_but_present' is a mild default but ED-0001 mentions missing raising hand, plausibly thin.

per_column.name: student_engagement_level
per_column.rationale: Engagement is a core outcome-adjacent axis to correlate with satisfaction and interventions. Well grounded: ED-0002 show up on time -> highly_engaged; ED-0005 cameras off/silent -> disengaged; ED-0003 crying/logged out -> disengaged. ED-0001 'passively_compliant' is a reasonable read of a frustrated but attending student.

per_column.name: subject_remote_fit
per_column.rationale: Captures how well a subject translates to remote delivery — a genuine grouping axis for targeting improvements. Values track the text: algebra whiteboard freezes -> low_fit, kitchen-chemistry works -> high_fit, discussion-based juniors -> low_fit. Somewhat conflated with tech issues vs true subject fit but broadly warranted.

judge.rationale: All six columns provide distinct, actionable axes (teaching quality, differentiation, format, peer learning, engagement, subject fit) that directly serve the query on improving learning satisfaction; none are near-constant or trivially redundant. Source groundedness is generally strong — most values are sound extractions or warranted categorizations of the open responses. Minor unwarranted specifics appear (e.g. 'moderate_office_hours' inventing office hours, and a couple 'mixed' format labels where the text describes a single modality), and some low-evidence default categories, lowering groundedness modestly but not indicating systematic fabrication.
